excerpt: Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy block creators in dozens of countries. Here is the sovereign infrastructure that works everywhere they do not.

content.text: If you're a digital creator in Nigeria, trying to sell plugins online without a payment processor is a real pain caused by Stripe's country restrictions. But you're not just limited by Stripe – other platforms like Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle also exclude certain countries. Here's the full infrastructure guide to understand your options, their strengths and weaknesses, and which one is best suited for your situation.
What Each Option Actually Offers

Gumroad, a popular platform for creators, offers a simple way to sell digital products, but its availability is limited in countries like Nigeria, Ghana, and Pakistan. Stripe, a payment processor, provides a wide range of tools for businesses, but its country restrictions lock out creators in many regions. Meanwhile, Lemon Squeezy offers a more comprehensive solution for digital sellers, but its fees can be steep for high-volume sales.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Gumroad requires a bank account, which is often unavailable in restricted countries, making it difficult for creators to access their payouts. Stripe's country restrictions mean that creators in certain regions can't even use the platform. Lemon Squeezy, on the other hand, claims to support creators in restricted countries, but its fees can be unpredictable, making it a less reliable option.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

NOWPayments operates as a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 cryptocurrencies including Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT on multiple chains, Solana, BNB on Binance Smart Chain, and Tron. When a buyer initiates payment, NOWPayments creates a unique payment address for that specific transaction. It monitors the blockchain in real time. When payment confirms on-chain, it fires a webhook to your configured endpoint automatically. The 0.5% fee is the only cost — no monthly fee, no setup fee, no revenue share, no payout schedule. Funds go directly to the wallet addresses you configure. COREMERCH never touches your wallet or your funds at any point.
COREMERCH's sovereign digital commerce stacks are built on free and open-source tools, making them a more secure and cost-effective option for creators in restricted countries.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Gumroad provides limited automation features, making it difficult for creators to manage their sales and deliveries efficiently. Stripe offers more advanced automation features, but its ownership model is unclear, making it difficult for creators to control their data and assets. Meanwhile, Lemon Squeezy offers a range of automation features, but its lack of transparency around ownership makes it a less secure option.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you're a digital creator in a restricted country, looking for a simple solution that's easy to set up, Gumroad might be a good starting point. However, if you're looking for more advanced automation features and a transparent ownership model, you may want to consider a sovereign digital commerce stack, like the one offered by COREMERCH, which provides a permanent structural alternative at the base layer.
